verdict.rationale: Homebrew ships its own registry: homebrew-core formulae with prebuilt bottles, casks for apps, fonts and plugins, and taps for extra repositories, with a JSON API listing all current formulae and casks. Community users say it has many more packages than MacPorts, updates versions quickly, and uses automation that bumps versions automatically. Missing for 10: no quantified registry size in first-party evidence, and isolated reports of version lag (e.g. Elixir 1.20, a llama.cpp tap) temper the 'actively maintained' claim.

support.subject: As a developer, I can install almost anything I need from a large, actively maintained package registry or repository

citations.quote: Homebrew installs the command-line tools and applications you need across macOS, Linux and WSL.
Casks are package definitions that install upstream pre-built binaries such as applications, fonts and plugins.
The `brew tap` command adds repositories that Homebrew can use for formulae, casks and external commands.
List the `brew info --json` output for all current Homebrew/homebrew-core formulae or Homebrew/homebrew-cask casks.
brew had and has many more packages available, brew updates versions more quickly
